TASK ID: exact-cover-to-sat

USER REQUEST:
Write a polynomial-time reduction from Exact Cover to SAT. problems.py defines both problems: SOURCE is Exact Cover and TARGET is SAT. The SOURCE and TARGET class docstrings give the exact instance formats, yes-conditions and edge cases.

PROBLEM DEFINITIONS (the SOURCE and TARGET docstrings from problems.py, complete as given here):

SOURCE = ExactCover
Exact Cover.

Instance: {"universe_size": u, "sets": [[element, ...], ...]}
  * The universe is the elements 0..u-1.
  * Each set lists distinct elements of the universe, in any order. A set
    may be empty, and the same set may appear more than once.

Yes iff some of the sets contain every element of the universe exactly
once: the chosen sets are pairwise disjoint and their union is the whole
universe.

Edge cases: u = 0 is yes (choose no sets). Empty sets never matter. Two
copies of the same non-empty set can never both be chosen.

TARGET = Sat
SAT (CNF satisfiability).

Instance: {"num_vars": m, "clauses": [[literal, ...], ...]}
  * Variables are 1..m. A literal is +v (v is true) or -v (v is false).
  * A clause is a list of any number of literals, including none.
    Literals may repeat, and a clause may contain both v and -v.
  * Literal order inside a clause and clause order do not matter. The
    same clause may appear more than once.
  * Variables need not all appear in a clause.

Yes iff some assignment of true/false to variables 1..m makes every
clause contain at least one true literal.

Edge cases: a formula with no clauses is satisfiable (yes). An empty
clause [] can never be satisfied, so any formula containing one is no.

INPUT FILES: ["problems.py"]
WORKING DIRECTORY: /tmp/reduction-fk8p_p7y
All input files are in this directory; run every command from it and write your files here. problems.py provides SOURCE and TARGET with validate(instance) only. It has NO solvers and NO instance generators.

REQUIRED OUTPUT: create reduce.py in the workspace, defining
    reduce(instance) -> instance
It takes an instance of the source problem and returns an instance of the target problem, both in the formats documented in problems.py. The answer to the returned instance must be yes exactly when the answer to the input instance is yes, and reduce must run in polynomial time. Do not call the brute-force solvers inside reduce.

Before submitting, check your reduction. problems.py has no solvers, so first write your own brute-force solvers for both problems from the definitions above. Then write tests in test_reduce.py that compare your solvers' answers on many small source instances and their reductions, run them, and revise until the tests pass. Finally write verdict.json as {"verified": true or false, "tests_run": <int>, "tests_passed": <int>}, where verified is true only if all of your tests pass. Then submit.

def validate_graph(instance: Instance) -> None:
    """Check the "n" and "edges" fields of a graph instance."""
    n = instance.get("n")
    require_int(n, "n", minimum=0)
    edges = instance.get("edges")
    require(isinstance(edges, list), "edges must be a list")
    seen: set[frozenset[int]] = set()
    for edge in edges:
        require(
            isinstance(edge, list) and len(edge) == 2,
            f"each edge must be a list [u, v], got {edge!r}",
        )
        u, v = edge
        require(is_int(u) and is_int(v), f"edge endpoints must be ints, got {edge!r}")
        require(0 <= u < n and 0 <= v < n, f"edge {edge!r} has a vertex outside 0..{n - 1}")

    require(isinstance(clauses, list), "clauses must be a list")

        require(isinstance(clause, list), f"each clause must be a list, got {clause!r}")
        for literal in clause:
            require(is_int(literal), f"literals must be ints, got {literal!r}")
            require(
                literal != 0 and abs(literal) <= num_vars,
                f"literal {literal} is outside ±1..±{num_vars}",
            )

    require(isinstance(numbers, list), "numbers must be a list")

        require(is_int(number), f"numbers must be ints, got {number!r}")
        require(number >= 0, f"numbers must be >= 0, got {number}")

    Instance: {"universe_size": u, "sets": [[element, ...], ...]}

    universe.

    Edge cases: u = 0 is yes (choose no sets). Empty sets never matter. Two
    copies of the same non-empty set can never both be chosen.
    """

    name = 'Exact Cover'

    @classmethod
    def validate(cls, instance: object) -> None:
        validate_set_system(instance, {"universe_size", "sets"})


class Sat:
    """SAT (CNF satisfiability).

    Instance: {"num_vars": m, "clauses": [[literal, ...], ...]}

      * Variables need not all appear in a clause.

    Yes iff some assignment of true/false to variables 1..m makes every
    clause contain at least one true literal.

    Edge cases: a formula with no clauses is satisfiable (yes). An empty
    clause [] can never be satisfied, so any formula containing one is no.
    """

    name = 'SAT'

    @classmethod
    def validate(cls, instance: object) -> None:
        require_keys(instance, {"num_vars", "clauses"})
        assert isinstance(instance, dict)
        validate_cnf(instance["clauses"], instance["num_vars"])

"""Polynomial-time reduction from Exact Cover to SAT.

Source (ExactCover): {"universe_size": u, "sets": [[element, ...], ...]}
Target (Sat):         {"num_vars": m, "clauses": [[literal, ...], ...]}

Construction
------------
Introduce one boolean variable x_i for every set i (variables 1..len(sets)).

* Covering: for every universe element e, add the clause
      [x_i for every set i containing e]
  This forces at least one chosen set to contain e.

* Disjointness: for every pair of distinct sets i < j that share at least
  one element, add the clause [-x_i, -x_j].
  This forbids choosing two sets that overlap.

A satisfying assignment selects exactly the sets whose variable is true.
Every element is covered (covering clauses) and no two selected sets overlap
(disjointness clauses), so the selected sets form an exact cover.  Conversely
any exact cover yields a satisfying assignment by setting its sets true.

Edge cases
----------
* u = 0: no covering clauses; if sets are non-empty the instance is invalid
  anyway (elements must be < 0), so all sets are empty and there are no
  overlap clauses either.  The formula has no clauses and is satisfiable,
  matching "u = 0 is yes".
* Empty sets: their variable never occurs in a clause, so it is free and
  never affects satisfiability, matching "empty sets never matter".
* Duplicate non-empty sets: they overlap, so the disjointness clause forbids
  choosing both, matching "two copies of the same non-empty set can never
  both be chosen".
* An element contained in no set produces the empty clause [], which is
  unsatisfiable, correctly making the instance a "no".
"""

from __future__ import annotations


def reduce(instance: dict) -> dict:
    """Return a SAT instance that is satisfiable iff the Exact Cover
    instance has an exact cover."""
    universe_size = instance["universe_size"]
    sets = instance["sets"]
    n = len(sets)

    clauses: list[list[int]] = []

    # Covering clauses: at least one set containing each element must be chosen.
    # For each element collect the indices of sets that contain it.
    containing: list[list[int]] = [[] for _ in range(universe_size)]
    for index, subset in enumerate(sets):
        for element in subset:
            containing[element].append(index)

    for element in range(universe_size):
        # Clause of positive literals (index + 1).  May be empty, which
        # correctly makes the formula unsatisfiable when no set covers it.
        clauses.append([index + 1 for index in containing[element]])

    # Disjointness clauses: forbid choosing two sets that share an element.
    # For each element, every pair of sets containing it must not both be
    # chosen.  Emitting these per element avoids an O(n^2) pairwise scan.
    for element in range(universe_size):
        indices = containing[element]
        for a in range(len(indices)):
            for b in range(a + 1, len(indices)):
                i = indices[a]
                j = indices[b]
                clauses.append([-(i + 1), -(j + 1)])

    return {"num_vars": n, "clauses": clauses}
EOF

"""Tests for the Exact Cover -> SAT reduction.

Contains brute-force solvers written from the problem definitions, a random
instance generator, and checks that the reduction preserves the answer.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import itertools
import random

from problems import ExactCover, Sat
from reduce import reduce


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Brute-force solvers

def solve_exact_cover(instance: dict) -> bool:
    """True iff some subfamily of sets exactly covers 0..u-1."""
    u = instance["universe_size"]
    sets = instance["sets"]
    n = len(sets)
    target = (1 << u) - 1
    # Try every subset of the sets.
    for mask in range(1 << n):
        union = 0
        ok = True
        for i in range(n):
            if mask & (1 << i):
                s = 0
                for e in sets[i]:
                    s |= 1 << e
                if union & s:  # overlap -> not disjoint
                    ok = False
                    break
                union |= s
        if ok and union == target:
            return True
    return False


def solve_sat(instance: dict) -> bool:
    """True iff some assignment satisfies every clause."""
    m = instance["num_vars"]
    clauses = instance["clauses"]
    for bits in range(1 << m):
        assignment = [(bits >> v) & 1 for v in range(m)]  # index v -> var v+1
        good = True
        for clause in clauses:
            if not any(
                (assignment[abs(lit) - 1] == 1) == (lit > 0) for lit in clause
            ):
                good = False
                break
        if good:
            return True
    return False


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Random instance generator

def random_exact_cover(rng: random.Random, max_u: int = 4, max_sets: int = 5) -> dict:
    u = rng.randint(0, max_u)
    n = rng.randint(0, max_sets)
    sets = []
    for _ in range(n):
        size = rng.randint(0, u)
        subset = rng.sample(range(u), size) if u > 0 else []
        sets.append(subset)
    return {"universe_size": u, "sets": sets}


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Tests

def test_edge_cases() -> int:
    passed = 0
    cases = [
        {"universe_size": 0, "sets": []},
        {"universe_size": 0, "sets": [[], []]},
        {"universe_size": 1, "sets": []},
        {"universe_size": 1, "sets": [[]]},
        {"universe_size": 1, "sets": [[0]]},
        {"universe_size": 1, "sets": [[0], [0]]},
        {"universe_size": 2, "sets": [[0], [1]]},
        {"universe_size": 2, "sets": [[0, 1]]},
        {"universe_size": 3, "sets": [[0, 1], [1, 2], [2, 0]]},
        {"universe_size": 3, "sets": [[0, 1], [2]]},
        {"universe_size": 3, "sets": [[0, 1], [1, 2], [0, 2], [0, 1, 2]]},
    ]
    for inst in cases:
        ExactCover.validate(inst)
        out = reduce(inst)
        Sat.validate(out)
        a = solve_exact_cover(inst)
        b = solve_sat(out)
        assert a == b, (inst, out, a, b)
        passed += 1
    return passed


def test_random(trials: int = 3000) -> int:
    rng = random.Random(12345)
    passed = 0
    for _ in range(trials):
        inst = random_exact_cover(rng)
        ExactCover.validate(inst)
        out = reduce(inst)
        Sat.validate(out)
        a = solve_exact_cover(inst)
        b = solve_sat(out)
        assert a == b, (inst, out, a, b)
        passed += 1
    return passed


def test_exhaustive_small() -> int:
    """Exhaustively enumerate all set systems for tiny universes."""
    passed = 0
    for u in range(0, 4):
        all_subsets = []
        for r in range(u + 1):
            all_subsets.extend(itertools.combinations(range(u), r))
        all_subsets = [list(c) for c in all_subsets]
        # All families of up to 3 sets drawn from the power set.
        for n in range(0, 4):
            for family in itertools.product(all_subsets, repeat=n):
                inst = {"universe_size": u, "sets": [list(s) for s in family]}
                ExactCover.validate(inst)
                out = reduce(inst)
                Sat.validate(out)
                a = solve_exact_cover(inst)
                b = solve_sat(out)
                assert a == b, (inst, out, a, b)
                passed += 1
    return passed


if __name__ == "__main__":
    total = 0
    total += test_edge_cases()
    total += test_random()
    total += test_exhaustive_small()
    print(f"all tests passed: {total}")
